meetings.title: Special Durham City Council Meeting Jan 10, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a special meeting on January 10, 2018 dedicated exclusively to hearing public testimony in support of the seven finalists for the vacant At-Large City Council seat. Mayor Steve Schewel established ground rules allocating 15 minutes of speaker time per candidate in alphabetical order, with bilingual Spanish-English interpretation provided and translation pauses excluded from each candidate's clock. Supporters addressed Council sequentially on behalf of finalists Shayla Arias, Javiera Caballero, Pierce Freelon, Karen Haldeman, Sheila Huggins, Carl Rist, and Pilar Rocha-Goldberg. No formal votes or council deliberations occurred, as Mayor Schewel reminded attendees that 45-minute candidate interviews would take place the following evening and the appointment vote would be held on January 16.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Process Ground Rules, and Bilingual Interpretation Setup
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel welcomed the seven finalists and members of the public, setting ground rules requiring positive advocacy without criticizing other candidates and granting each finalist 15 minutes for designated supporters to speak. Staff and interpreters Iris Ramirez and Jorge explained headset channels and live Spanish-English interpretation, with the City Clerk pausing the 15-minute clock during interpretation.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Shayla Arias
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters including Kim Swanson, Beth Messersmith, Jessica Burroughs, Tara Lemus, Jessica Berryman, and Yessenia Alvarez spoke on behalf of Shayla Arias. Speakers highlighted her journey as a naturalized citizen, her advocacy with MomsRising and Smart Start, her Latino community outreach nights on mental health and immigration resources, and her personal resilience.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Javiera Caballero
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters spoke in both English and Spanish on behalf of Javiera Caballero, emphasizing her experience as a teacher in Durham and her PTA presidency at Club Boulevard Elementary. Testimony praised her ability to stretch limited budgets, her partnership to bring Communities in Schools resources to students, and her ethical advocacy for immigrant and working families.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Pierce Freelon
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters including Chris Tiffany, Chris Massenburg, Angie Santiago, Jewel Taylor, Elizabeth Turnbull, George Roberson, Gabriel Eng-Goetz, and Michelle Gonzalez-Green spoke on behalf of Pierce Freelon. Speakers highlighted his independence from political action committees, his nonprofit youth leadership and fundraising work, and his advocacy on downtown gentrification.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Karen Haldeman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including Mayor Moss and Andrew Stillwell testified in support of Karen Haldeman. They cited her committee work, involvement with African American Heritage Day, strong communication skills, and collaborative encouragement of other candidates and women in civic life.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Sheila Huggins
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters spoke on behalf of Sheila Huggins, describing her grassroots neighborhood engagement in Northeast Central Durham, including Play Streets and Partners Against Crime meetings, as well as her broader civic organizing and advocacy across North Carolina.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Carl Rist
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel introduced the 15-minute public comment segment for finalist Carl Rist, during which supporters addressed Council regarding his qualifications for the vacant At-Large seat.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment in Support of Finalist Pilar Rocha-Goldberg
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters including Sonia Rodriguez, Celestino Morales, Evan McDonald, and others testified in Spanish and English on behalf of Pilar Rocha-Goldberg. Speakers emphasized her eight years of nonprofit leadership, her wisdom and support for youth and families, and her deep roots in the community.

agenda_items.title: Closing Remarks and Appointment Schedule Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel thanked the Spanish interpreters, City Clerk staff, speakers, and all seven finalists, noting the difficulty of the council's upcoming choice. He reminded the public of the 45-minute candidate interviews scheduled for the following night at 5:00 p.m. and the appointment vote set for January 16 at 5:30 p.m., adjourning the meeting at 9:09 p.m.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 2, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its first regular meeting of 2018 on January 2, the six-member Durham City Council issued ceremonial proclamations recognizing January 2018 as National Mentoring Month and honoring the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. During announcements, Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton reflected on attending a Bull City United Week of Peace vigil and urged residents to bring proactive gun-violence prevention ideas to Council chambers. Council unanimously approved 6-0 the consent agenda (excluding pulled Item 7), covering the FY 2018-19 budget schedule, HUD grant amendments, Jackson-Pettigrew Street affordable housing financing, bicycle facility design, hydrant meter rates, and the November 2017 bid report. After Transportation Director Terry Bellamy answered a question confirming that federal minority- and women-owned business rules governed pulled Item 7, Council unanimously passed 6-0 the NCDOT grant project ordinance for the downtown transportation study.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led a moment of silent meditation, followed by Boy Scout Troop 461 leading the Pledge of Allegiance at the invitation of Council Member Charlie Reece. The Clerk called the roll, confirming all six seated council members were present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Declaring January 2018 as National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece read a proclamation signed by Mayor Schewel designating January 2018 as National Mentoring Month in Durham. Doran Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation accepted the proclamation alongside representatives of My Brother's Keeper Durham, Movement of Youth / Mentors Carolina, and Men of Vision in McDougald Terrace.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Honoring the Life of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read a proclamation honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and recalling his visits to Durham between 1960 and 1964. Pastor William Lucas, Chair of the Durham Martin Luther King Jr. Steering Committee, accepted the proclamation and noted the 50th anniversary of Dr. King's assassination and upcoming MLK commemorative events.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements: Gun Violence Vigil and Community Advocacy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton recognized Bull City United for hosting a Week of Peace vigil for gunfire victims and acknowledged Durham's progress on homicides while stressing continuing challenges with gunfire. He urged activists and residents to come to Council chambers with concrete recommendations to prevent gun violence rather than waiting until after tragedies occur.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Records Retention, FY18-19 Budget Schedule, HUD Grants, Jackson-Pettigrew Housing, Bike Design, Hydrant Rates, Bid Report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda, including council minutes, municipal record retention schedule amendments, the FY 18-19 budget development schedule, FY 2017-18 HUD grant amendments (CDBG, HOME, ESG, and HOPWA), subordinate financing for the Jackson-Pettigrew Street development with Self-Help Ventures Fund and DHIC, Inc., a bicycle facility design master agreement, Chapter 15 hydrant meter deposit and rental rate amendments, and the November 2017 bid report. Item 7 was pulled at a council member's request, and the remaining consent items passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham and NCDOT Grant Project Ordinance for Downtown Transportation Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda for clarification, a council member asked why the agenda memo stated the agreement was not reviewed for compliance with Durham's Equal Business Opportunity ordinance. Transportation Director Terry Bellamy explained that because the study uses federal funding, it follows federal minority- and women-owned business regulations rather than the local ordinance, and clarified that an RFQ panel was reviewing submittals while this ordinance simply established grant funding authority; Council approved the item 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3-6, 8-10, excluding pulled Item 7)
votes.notes: Six seated members present prior to filling the vacant At-Large seat.
votes.discussion_detail: After reading the consent agenda and pulling Item 7 at a council member's request, Mayor Schewel entertained a motion to approve the remaining consent items (Items 1, 3-6, and 8-10), which was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 18, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The six-member Durham City Council unanimously approved 6-0 the consent agenda—including GoDurham replacement buses, HOPWA and Enterprise Community Partners contract amendments, and multiple pedestrian and waterline projects—while receiving public comment on the FY 2018-19 Annual Action Plan amid questions from Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and DeDreana Freeman over shifting CDBG and ESG homelessness dollars toward rapid rehousing and future Dedicated Housing Fund allocations. Council also voted 6-0 on all land-use items, re-designating land around the Venable Center as a local historic landmark, rezoning 5275 North Roxboro Street to Commercial General with a Development Plan, and approving the 93-acre Sagewood and Nichols Farm consolidated annexation. Additionally, Council unanimously adopted 6-0 a resolution supporting the federal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program and approved 6-0 the timeline, candidate questionnaire, and interview procedures to fill the vacant At-Large Council seat.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Recognitions, and NC Commission of Inquiry on Torture Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Troop 451 led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the City Clerk called the roll with all six seated council members present. Mayor Steve Schewel recognized neighborhood health and GirlTrek volunteers and read a proclamation for NC Stop Torture Now regarding the North Carolina Commission of Inquiry on Torture (NCCIT) findings on rendition flights at Johnston County and Global TransPark.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and City Clerk reported no priority items. City Attorney Patrick Baker notified Council and the public that three documents produced at the December 13 Council Procedures Subcommittee meeting were added to General Business Agenda Item 2 regarding the City Council vacancy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Duke Energy Intervention, HOPWA Amendment, GoDurham Buses, Water/Sewer & Pedestrian Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda titles covering intervention in Duke Energy case E-7 Sub 1146, the Appearance Commission interlocal renewal, a HOPWA contract amendment, Enterprise Community Partners Phase 2, GoDurham replacement buses, Southeast Regional Lift Station engineering, a 2-inch waterline replacement contract, Neighborhood Compass management, North Duke Street/NC 54/South Street pedestrian improvements, and Odyssey Drive and Alpine Road culvert replacements.

agenda_items.title: FY 2018-19 Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Moved first on the General Business Agenda, Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conaway-Jans (ph.) outlined projected HUD entitlements ($1.8M CDBG, $800k HOME, $160k ESG, and $328k HOPWA) ahead of the May 15, 2018 submission. Homeless service providers including Urban Ministries of Durham, Families Moving Forward, and Outstretched Hands—along with Council Members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman, and Mayor Steve Schewel—questioned eliminating ~$130,000 in CDBG homelessness funding and dedicating ESG entirely to rapid rehousing prior to Council review of the Focus Strategies report and Dedicated Housing Fund budget proposals.

agenda_items.title: Venable Center Local Historic Landmark Designation (LD170001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Karla Rosenberg presented Case LD170001 to re-designate land associated with the Venable Center at South Roxboro and East Pettigrew Streets after a 2016 subdivision/recombination inadvertently stripped landmark status from the front courtyard and small annex parking lot, estimating $3,287 in annual city tax revenue impact ($7,650 combined city-county). Applicant representative Charlie Yokely of the McAdams Company confirmed the omission was an unintended clerical overlap.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 5275 North Roxboro Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jamie Sunyak presented a request to rezone 1.31 acres (a vacant Burger King site) in the Eno River Basin Overlay from Commercial Neighborhood to Commercial General with a Development Plan capping floor area at 10,000 sq ft and committing to a bus pullout shelter and TIP U-516 right-of-way dedication, unanimously recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission. Applicant engineer Tim Sivers and owner Dale Reynolds described plans for a water-conserving express car wash paying at least $11/hour plus benefits and employing people with disabilities, while Council Member DeDreana Freeman flagged potential competition with nearby car washes.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Sagewood and Nichols Farm
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jacob Wiggins presented Highland Falls Raleigh LLC's request for utility extension agreements, voluntary annexation effective December 31, 2017, and exact-translation Rural Residential (RR) initial zoning for two contiguous parcels totaling ~93 acres along Doc Nichols Road. Staff noted water/sewer capacity and positive fiscal buildout impact, and confirmed in response to Mark-Anthony Middleton that including Doc Nichols Road right-of-way creates donut holes because an intervening property owner declined annexation.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting the Federal Temporary Protected Status (TPS) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson introduced and read a resolution urging the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to renew TPS for Nicaragua and Haiti and continue protections for the estimated 320,000 national and 13,000 North Carolina TPS holders. Eliazar Posada of El Centro Hispano and Jose Fidel Campos-Sorto of the North Carolina Salvadoran Association thanked Council while urging continued concrete local support.

agenda_items.title: City Council At-Large Vacancy Timeline, Questionnaire, and Interview Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker reviewed the Procedures Subcommittee recommendations to adopt the vacancy timeline, revised candidate questionnaire (with formatting additions noted by Council Member Vernetta Alston), and applicant interview rules and procedures. On Council Member Charlie Reece's recommendation, Council deferred choosing the final voting/selection method to Thursday's work session.

votes.item_title: Receive Public Comments on FY 2018-19 Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing (Item 18)
votes.notes: No funding allocations were adopted at this first needs hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: Following an extended public hearing on CDBG and ESG homelessness service funding allocations, Director Reginald Johnson reminded Mayor Schewel that Council needed to formally vote to receive the public comments. A motion and second passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Designating Venable Center Land as a Local Historic Landmark (LD170001, Item 15)
votes.discussion_detail: After staff and applicant testimony clarified that only the historic building parcel's front courtyard and annex lot—not the rear redevelopment parking lot—were being re-designated, Council closed the hearing and voted 6-0 to adopt the landmark ordinance.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for 5275 North Roxboro Street Zoning Map Change (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Following questions from Council Member DeDreana Freeman regarding local competition and wage/disability hiring commitments from applicant Dale Reynolds, Council closed the public hearing and unanimously adopted the consistency statement 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Amending UDO Zoning Map for 5275 North Roxboro Street (Item 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the zoning map change from CN to CG(D) with a 10,000 sq ft maximum floor area on a 6-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Annexation Ordinances and Authorize Utility Extension Agreements for Sagewood and Nichols Farm (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: After staff answered Mark-Anthony Middleton's question about donut holes along Doc Nichols Road, Council closed the public hearing and approved the consolidated motion to adopt the annexation ordinances and authorize utility extension agreements 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Sagewood and Nichols Farm Initial Zoning (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the comprehensive plan consistency statement 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Initial Zoning Ordinance (RR) for Sagewood and Nichols Farm (Item 17)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the UDO amendment establishing Rural Residential (RR) initial zoning for the 93-acre annexation 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Supporting the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) Program (Item 23)
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read and moved the resolution supporting TPS renewal, with public speakers from El Centro Hispano and the NC Salvadoran Association endorsing the measure. Council passed the resolution 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt City Council At-Large Vacancy Timeline, Candidate Questionnaire, and Interview Rules and Procedures (Item 2)
votes.notes: Final vote administered by the retiring City Clerk after 33 years of service.
votes.discussion_detail: After confirming with City Attorney Patrick Baker that all three Procedures Subcommittee attachments (including Vernetta Alston's nominal formatting updates to the questionnaire) could be adopted together while deferring the selection voting method to Thursday's work session, Council approved the motion 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec 4, 2017
meetings.executive_summary: The December 4, 2017 Durham City Council organizational meeting began with certification of the 2017 municipal election results and farewell tributes to outgoing Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Eddie Davis and Don Moffitt. Newly elected Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, Vernetta Alston, and DeDreana Freeman took the oath of office, after which the six-member council unanimously elected Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore 6-0. Following a brief recess, Council passed the consent agenda 6-0 and unanimously voted 6-0 after a public hearing to approve Public Finance Authority multifamily housing revenue bonds for the Lynn Haven Apartments affordable housing project.

agenda_items.title: Election Certification and Farewells for Outgoing Mayor and Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and received certified 2017 municipal election results. Council and staff honored outgoing members Don Moffitt, Eddie Davis, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Mayor Bill Bell with plaques and reflections on their tenure covering affordable housing, transit, and financial stewardship.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In of Newly Elected Mayor and Council Members and Inaugural Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Newly elected Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, Vernetta Alston, and DeDreana Freeman, along with Mayor Steve Schewel, took their oaths of office and delivered inaugural remarks thanking outgoing leaders, families, and voters while outlining their shared vision for Durham.

agenda_items.title: Election and Swearing-In of Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece moved to designate Council Member Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore for the City of Durham. Council approved the designation 6-0, and Johnson took the oath of office surrounded by her family.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (DPAC Oversight, DHA Reappointment, FY17 CAFR, Water Audit, Housing & BPAC Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a 10-minute recess, Mayor Schewel read consent items covering a DPAC Oversight Committee appointment, Durham Housing Authority Board reappointment, the FY 2017 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, a Water Management meter disconnect/reconnect audit, a county revenue-reimbursement interlocal agreement, Piedmont-Reynolds loan amendments with Durham Community Land Trustees, BPAC reauthorization, water deposit ordinance updates, the October 2017 bid report, and a Davis Park East median sign license.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution Approving Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds — Lynn Haven Apartments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson presented a resolution approving the Public Finance Authority's issuance of multifamily housing revenue bonds for the Lynn Haven Apartments affordable housing project. In response to Mayor Schewel's inquiry, developer legal counsel Eric Prostell addressed accompanying housing tax credits, and with no public speakers, Council unanimously adopted the bond resolution 6-0.

votes.item_title: Designate Council Member Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: Mayor Schewel's vacated At-Large seat remained vacant pending the council appointment process.
votes.discussion_detail: At Mayor Schewel's invitation, Council Member Charlie Reece moved to designate Jillian Johnson as Mayor Pro Tempore, which was seconded and approved 6-0.

votes.item_title: Resolution Approving Issuance of Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds for Lynn Haven Apartments (Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Community Development Director Reginald Johnson's staff report and developer counsel Eric Prostell's response regarding tax credits, no members of the public signed up to speak; Council closed the hearing and unanimously adopted the resolution 6-0.
